text:
alex: FYI prod-13b (q8) started showing a p99 latency bump ~1h after the kernel roll. very pronounced for streaming short-turn chat flows. anyone seen this pattern?

marta: @alex saw the alert, digging in. p50 fine, p95 slight, p99 +120ms. looks correlated with kernel selection falling back to the scalar/scattered fastpath.

suresh: ssh'd into a node and grabbed perf counters. rx: kernel-switches spiked during the bump. KV cache hit-rate stable. suspect quantized kernel scan-backoff is mis-triggering when sequence lengths vary.

ben: can you paste the kernel selector logs? curious which heuristic flipped.

alex: pasted snippet from node (trimmed):
```
2026-03-18T09:12:31Z kernel_selector INFO selected kernel: q8_scatter_fastpath
2026-03-18T09:12:31Z kernel_selector DEBUG fallback probe: scan_backoff=1.6, seq_var=0.34, p99_latency_prev=11ms
2026-03-18T09:12:31Z runtime WARNING switching to q8_scalar_slowpath due to backoff threshold
```

marta: that backoff value (1.6) is higher than our usual 1.2 threshold. looks like the scan_backoff multiplier logic used an old default for this model config.

perf-bot: profiling summary for thread 3723456789:
- p99 delta: +118ms
- top CPU frames: kernel_dispatch -> q8_scalar_slowpath -> attention_kv_load
- observed increased memcpy from KV cache spill -> cpu fallback

suresh: I grabbed a microprofile while reproducing:
```
Model: Llama-3-13B (hidden=4096 heads=32 rmsnorm)
Config: rope_theta=10000, chat_template=short-prefix
Batch: mixed (1-3), streaming enabled, quant=q8_0
Observations:
  - frequent small seq churn (avg 24 tokens) triggers selector to prefer scalar path
  - KV cache entries ok, but stride mismatch causes extra memcopy for quant kernels
```

ben: stride mismatch? you mean headkv layout not aligning to 32-byte vector lanes in q8 kernel?

suresh: exactly. For this model hidden_size/head_dim combo we have head_dim=128 which is fine, but our RoPE tiling code uses a granularity derived from rope_theta bucketization. when rope_theta granularity doesn't align with the quant kernel's packing, we do an extra gather + memcpy before running the q8 kernel. that overhead kills p99 on short streaming responses.

alex: interesting. so not strictly KV miss, more layout conversion induced by rope granularity disparity. any quick mitigations?

marta: two options: 1) lower scan_backoff threshold so selector stays on the scatter fastpath longer for small sequences, 2) add a pre-check that verifies layout alignment before deciding to fallback. option 1 is fastest.

ben: we should also consider a lightweight cache of layout-converted prefixes to avoid repeated memcpy when chat template repeats the same prefix. chat_template=short-prefix causes many sessions to reuse same system prompt.

suresh: tried a prototype: keep a per-tenant small LRU of converted-kv for prefix lengths <= 64. saved ~40ms on p99 in local sim. code:
```
if prefix_len <= 64 and tenant_has_prefixed_cache:
    use_cached_converted_kv()
else:
    normal_compute()
```

perf-bot: sim numbers (local perf run): baseline p99=210ms, with layout-cache p99=170ms, with scan_backoff tweak p99=150ms.

alex: good gains. but layout-cache implies more memory and cache-key complexity. need to validate with multi-tenant eviction patterns.

marta: for short rollout: set scan_backoff default to 1.1 for Llama-2/3 q8 configs where head_dim % 64 == 0 and chat_template in [short-prefix, system-first]. This is narrow and reversible.

ben: +1. Also add a one-off telemetry gauge: count of selector-triggered layout-conversions per minute per model_version. want numbers for 24h after rollout.

suresh: I'll open a small PR with two commits: (A) scan_backoff default tweak + unit test, (B) add metric `runtime.layout_conversion.count` and tag `model,chat_template,tenant`.

alex: can we patch prod via canary on dedicated pool first? prefer 5% traffic on canary for 3 hours then 25% then global.

marta: agreed. I'll coordinate with oncall for the canary windows. also adding rollback alerts if p99 > baseline + 50ms or error rate increases.

ben: one more note for follow-up: we should audit our rope_theta heuristics across Llama-2/3 variants. for some sizes rope_theta defaulting to 10000 creates weird tiling for 4096 hidden dims; maybe we should recompute bucketization using head_dim alignments during model onboarding.

alex: created ticket INF-4921 to re-evaluate rope_theta granularity and the quant kernel packing interplay. tagging @marta @suresh.

marta: thanks. rolling the canary patch in ~30m. will post results. :rocket:

perf-bot: canary started at 2026-03-18T09:48:00Z on pool `dedicated-13b-canary` with 5% traffic. metrics stream hooked.

suresh: quick heads-up — after applying scan_backoff tweak in canary we saw immediate p99 drop to baseline within 10 minutes. continuing to monitor.

ben: great. once stable let's schedule the rope_theta audit as a follow-up spike.

alex: thanks all. saving logs & perf dumps to /var/log/runtime/3723456789/ for the ticket.

marta: closing the loop once canary reaches 3h. :white_check_mark:
